To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dietary fiber (DF), especially soluble DF (SDF) has a negative effect on energy and nutrient digestibilities.
dietary fiber from different feed ingredients has different effects on digestion, fermentation and gut health of pigs.

DF from different feedstuffs are fermented differently in the GIT of pigs, and this affects the digestion of other nutrients, production and utilization of fermentation metabolites, and microbial community in different sections of GIT.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of different types of dietary fiber (DF; insoluble, soluble and resistant) on the utilization of nutrients, fermentation characteristics, production and utilization of short chain fatty acids (SCFA), microbial community and health of swine.

understanding the role of DF in the diet of swine on their physiological functions and gut environment, especially on the production and utilization of fermentation metabolites and their effects on the gut health of pigs.
the development of a new generation of feed ingredients with high content and quality of DF and other bioactive compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DF is a complex and heterogeneous fraction of feed ingredients and its utilization in the GIT of pigs is affected by its composition and fractions.
DF is a complex group of compounds with wide variations in their chemical composition, physico-chemical characteristics and their roles in the GIT of pigs.
the inclusion of DF in the diets of swine is beneficial to the animals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is a need for a better understanding of the roles of DF on the digestion, absorption, metabolism and utilization of nutrients in the GIT and the effects on the microbial community, gut health, and overall animal performance.
DF from feed ingredients can be used in pig diets to enhance gut health and to optimize the production of metabolites in GIT.
DF in the diet of swine is a complex mixture of compounds with different physico-chemical characteristics and biological activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DF is a complex and multifaceted feed ingredient.
DF from feed ingredients commonly used in pig feeding can be used as an effective tool to improve gut health and performance in pigs.
the type of DF in the diet can be selected based on its physico-chemical and fermentation characteristics to achieve the desired effects on gut health of pigs.
